strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds a bounded headless continuation RPC that validates aggregate progress state, selects one eligible runnable task in Rust, records decision evidence, and executes exactly one existing task.run path.
Consumes the M10.2 runtime-owned task.list progress_overview fingerprint, aggregate_sequence, nodes, and next actions as the authoritative continuation input.
Keeps task selection and admission in Rust, requires explicit authorize=true, and preserves the existing task.run permission and admission pipeline.
Allows controlled queued child tasks to be selected and run only through existing explicit child task.run admission, while excluding parent-join execution from M11.1.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with support from progress_visualization, runtime_permission_enforcement, and subtask_orchestration.
answers.new_capability: A caller can invoke headless.continue_once with authorize=true plus the expected progress fingerprint and aggregate sequence. The Rust runtime rejects stale progress, selects one eligible Created or controlled Queued task whose next action is run_task_explicitly, records bounded HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence, and executes exactly one existing task.run path.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M10.2 task.list exposes runnable task IDs but leaves selection policy, stale aggregate handling, and conversion to task.run in the caller. Direct task.run executes only a caller-selected task ID and cannot validate that selection against the expected aggregate progress state.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless controllers would still own task prioritization and stale-state checks outside Rust, leaving Brownie with progress visibility but no runtime-owned single-step continuation primitive.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M9.6 materialized selected index context, M10.1 exposed single-run progress snapshots, and M10.2 exposed aggregate task-set progress. M11.1 adds runtime-owned continuation control and task execution.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. This is a task-set operation that validates aggregate state, selects one eligible task, records decision evidence, and executes that task. Reusing task.run would keep selection policy outside the runtime.
answers.no_new_summary: Only bounded continuation result metadata is added as evidence of actual execution or stale/no-eligible rejection. It is not a report, digest, readiness surface, history, verdict, or selected-next-action preview.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime now owns one deterministic headless next-step selection and can execute exactly one selected task after stale-state validation and explicit authorization.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: It gives scheduled and headless callers a replay/stale guarded single-step continuation primitive before any autonomous loop, async executor, or scheduler is introduced.
answers.milestone_progress: M11 gains its first executable headless control slice. Later phases can build replay/recovery routing or bounded repeated continuation on top of this single-step contract.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M11.1 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm authorized runtime-owned continue-once execution, not another progress wrapper or VSIX-owned policy.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts authorize=true, expected_progress_fingerprint, expected_aggregate_sequence, and an optional bounded continuation_id
Missing or false authorize is rejected without HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded or TaskRunning evidence
Stale progress fingerprint or aggregate_sequence returns bounded stale_progress metadata and appends no HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded or TaskRunning evidence
When no eligible Created or controlled Queued runnable task exists, the runtime returns bounded no_eligible_task metadata and executes nothing
When eligible tasks exist, Rust selects exactly one deterministic candidate whose next action is run_task_explicitly
The runtime records bounded HeadlessContinuationDecisionRecorded evidence before TaskRunning for the selected task
The selected task executes through the existing task.run path and no fallback candidate is selected in the same request
Controlled Queued child tasks remain admitted only through existing queued-child provenance validation

Parent-join-ready completed parents, blocked tasks, terminal tasks, recovery retries, proposal apply, verifier expansion, shell/git/network/service actions, live observation, async scheduling, and loops are out of scope
VSIX adds only params/result validation and a thin client method; it does not infer task-selection policy

No raw prompt, provider response, selected file content, workspace file content, ledger payload, stdout, stderr, command string, environment value, raw request body, absolute path, canonical path, secret, or arbitrary percentage is stored or returned

Behavior tests verify created task execution, controlled queued child execution, missing authorization rejection, stale progress rejection, no-eligible no-op, parent-join exclusion, bounded decision evidence, and at-most-one task execution

test_tokens: creates a headless.continue_once request without owning selection policy

next_phase_after_m11_1: M11.2 Headless Continuation Replay And Recovery Routing
next_phase_candidate_notes: M11.2 should address lost-response replay or routing from failed one-step continuation into existing recovery/apply/verifier paths. It must not start as an async loop, scheduler, report wrapper, or live progress observer.
